flags.summary: Sales manager stated he looked up a prospect's personal credit and income data before the call and briefed the closer on it; the figures also contradicted what the prospect disclosed live an hour later.
evidence: He's got a strong driver, strong intent, and I looked up his financial data. He's got 10K credit, he's got 106K income, he's a total beginner, so he's in a good spot. Do your best.

flags.summary: Manager instructed reps to take a card on file with an assurance it will not be charged until an agreed date, noting the card can be run regardless once held.
evidence: Even if it's like a credit card commitment, even if they're like, I cannot run money, be like, cool, then we'll just take down the card on file and I won't run it until this day.
Because once the card's on file, we can technically just run it.

flags.summary: Manager instructed the team to apply a harder financial qualification to prospects based on their country of origin.
evidence: If they come from certain, like UAE is one of those countries where I probably wouldn't hard financially qualify too much. If somebody's coming from Egypt, yeah, I probably would, you know, like let them know a little bit harder about the investment, Kim.
if you have somebody from countries that it might be harder for them to afford things, just, like, let them know, you know? Just kind of give them a little bit of a harder FQ.

flags.summary: A prospect reported in writing that he was pressured and that his disclosed feelings about his father were used against him on a closing call; the coaching response addressed objection technique rather than the pressure.
evidence: he basically said that he didn't like at the end that he felt pushed and used the emotions about his father and so on. Yeah, so I technically burned him, but now we know.

You got the feedback. He gave you the feedback, too. We've clarified. know exactly what the thing is. And just got to do a better job of isolating the right objection and understanding where the person's coming from.

flags.summary: Manager stated payment plans are only offered where affordability is certain and improvised financial terms only when the prospect proposes them; the same afternoon a closer on this call improvised three unpublished lower price points for a prospect with zero income and zero savings.
evidence: I only sell people if I know for sure they can afford it and it's not going to put them in a tight spot when I offer payment plans and I do stuff like That's what I do.
the only time I ever do something financially for somebody that I'm like, whoa, that's not something I would do, is if they suggest it. Because I'm not here to play God.
I got to use the washroom really quick, and then I'm going to jump on with David and end the day with a couple sales here.

flags.summary: Manager taught deliberately withholding the deposit amount in order to gauge and then challenge the prospect's reaction.
evidence: I actually like to not tell them what the deposit is going to be and then see if they react terribly to it. And then I say, Hey dude, like I could have told you it was $1. Like what's going on?
Yeah. That's my favorite. They always look at me like, damn, you're right. You got me.

flags.summary: Prospect-facing text conversations are handled by an AI chatbot and read back by reps, with no disclosure of the automation mentioned anywhere in the meeting.
evidence: He messaged our AI bot that I already know everything from the first call. I only need to know the price.
Manny yesterday didn't show up, but well, he actually texted also our AI chat bot, and I didn't see that.

flags.summary: A results guarantee is taught as a closing rebuttal without any stated terms, conditions or scope.
evidence: Would you bring up also the performance guarantee at that point? Yeah, I would. I'd bring it up. I'd we're literally guaranteeing it.
When it comes to guaranteeing the results, like we do, Trevor's the best. And that's why the investment is what it is.

flags.summary: A pending close was being held out of the weekly numbers pending an international transfer, and the new deposit rule changes how commitments are logged mid-corpus.
evidence: I'm not going to count in that Jorge guy until the money's in the account, and that might not be until Friday.
We'll get a commitment because we can't put an onboarding call. Like moving forward, no onboarding calls go on the calendar unless we take a deposit.
